The main takeaway from our work is that

CD22Δ12, a truncated and functionably defective form of the CD22 protein, is encoded by aberrant mRNA arising due to a splicing defect caused by homozygous mutation within a 132bp segment of the intron between exons 13 and 14.

a splicing defect in the CD22 gene is associated with a profound change in the secondary structures of the pre-mRNA sequences, which in turn causes a profound change in splicing patterns and leads to a truncated and functionaly defective CD22 protein, which is associated with a unique gene expression signature, which in turn is associated with an aggressive clinical phenotype in infant leukemia patients.
CD22Δ12 is a pathogenic mechanism that causes a profound defect in the regulation of gene transcription in infant leukemic cells, leading to a unique leukemia-associated gene expression signature.
